subject: DPA discussion: onshore processing, deletion windows and backups
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.han@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme DPA redlines: residency + deletion windows

Olga, thanks for taking this on. Attached is Acme's annotated DPA (ACME-DPA-redline-v2.pdf). Two items we need clarity on before legal can sign: 1) Residency — we require processing and storage of Acme customer content to remain within EU data centers for EU accounts (including backups), and 2) Deletion — we need a clear, enforceable deletion and proof-of-destruction timeline. Our starting asks: primary data must be deleted within 30 days of request or termination, and backups must be overwritten within 90 days.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept onshore processing for the EU and provide contractual wording for the backup deletion guarantee? Also: please highlight what evidence/certs you can provide (SOC2, audit logs, KMS key access records).

Thanks —
Sarah Lee
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp

Attachment: ACME-DPA-redline-v2.pdf (annotated DPA, 42KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines: residency + deletion windows

Sarah — appreciate the clear redlines. I reviewed the attached PDF and looped in Engineering & Compliance to confirm feasibility. High level: Redwood can commit to EU-hosted processing and storage for accounts designated EU, and we have options for encryption and KMS integration. Where we need to negotiate is the backup deletion language: operationally, we do not perform per-request physical destruction of tape/snapshot images immediately — we typically rely on overwrites/retention windows. That said, I'm confident we can propose contract language that gives Acme a firm deletion SLA plus audit evidence.

Proposed next steps: 1) I will circulate a short response doc with counter-proposals for wording (attached: RDW-response-dpa-proposal.docx), 2) Vivek will provide a technical note on backups and key handling, and 3) if agreeable, we can propose compromise deletion timelines rather than the stark 30/90 split.

Two quick questions for Acme: a) do you require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for EU accounts or will Redwood-managed KMS (with per-account keys) satisfy you? b) should the DPA require physical certificate of destruction for storage media, or is an auditable overwrite + confirmation sufficient?

Cc'ing Vivek who will follow up with the technical details.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-response-dpa-proposal.docx (proposed clause language, 18KB)

From: Tom Han <tom.han@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, sarah.lee@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redlines: residency + deletion windows

Olga / Sarah — quick technical note from Acme Security. For our EU customers we require: 1) data at rest and in transit to remain in EU regions; 2) ability to audit key rotation events; and 3) that backups containing customer content be made unavailable within 30 days and cryptographically irrecoverable within 180 days.

The 'unavailable within 30 days' can be implemented by logical deletion + removal of decryption keys, but we need explicit contractual language that keys are destroyed/rotated in a way that prevents recovery, and we require confirmation within 30 days of deletion requests. An attestation or log extract is fine for now, but we will want to see proof during onboarding.

Regards,
Tom Han
Security Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, tom.han@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Technical note: backup lifecycle, KMS, and deletion guarantees

Tom / Olga — following up with specifics so legal teams can draft precise language. Summary below; I attached a matrix with retention categories. Attachment: backup-retention-matrix.csv; kms-integration-notes.pdf included.

1) Residency: Redwood can operate a geographically isolated tenant for EU-designated accounts. All primary storage, snapshots, and the default backup replication for that tenant will be restricted to EU regions (Frankfurt/Paris/Amsterdam) — no cross-region replication for that tenant unless explicitly enabled by the customer.

2) Backups & snapshots: our snapshot pipeline creates immutable block snapshots. Practical deletion flow: - Live deletion request (T0): application-layer objects are logically deleted from primary stores immediately. - Snapshot lifecycle: snapshots are retained according to snapshot policies; they become inaccessible to normal reads once we initiate wipe. - Crypto-erase: for encrypted snapshots, we can cryptographically render data irrecoverable by expiring or deleting the encryption keys (BYOK or Redwood-managed per-tenant keys). Key destruction achieves irrecoverability faster than physical overwrite in many cloud scenarios.

3) Suggested contractual wording alternatives (pick one):
- Option A (Customer-managed keys): "Customer may provide and control encryption keys; upon deletion request Redwood shall destroy access and provide key rotation logs within 30 days; backups will be cryptographically rendered irrecoverable within 30 days."
- Option B (Redwood-managed keys): "Redwood will manage per-tenant keys and upon deletion request shall render backups inaccessible within 30 days and cryptographically irrecoverable within 180 days; Redwood will provide key rotation and deletion logs within 30 days upon request."

4) Evidence & audit: Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report, KMS event logs, and a deletion confirmation package (log extracts + signed attestation). For EU residency we can provide network flow/region configuration screenshots and a short onboarding checklist.

5) Caveat: archived cold copies stored by third-party long-term archival providers (if enabled) may have separate overwrite schedules; we will surface these in the contract if applicable.

I attached technical notes with the exact log fields we can extract. Happy to walk through with your security team this week.

--Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: backup-retention-matrix.csv (snapshot timelines), kms-integration-notes.pdf (KMS event taxonomy)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.han@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical note: backup lifecycle, KMS, and deletion guarantees

Thanks Vivek — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from Legal/Security after reviewing the options:

- We prefer Option A (customer-managed keys) for EU accounts. Customer control over keys is a non-negotiable for this deal.
- We will accept a compromise on backup irrecoverability: 30 days to make backups inaccessible (logical + key-removal), 180 days for cryptographic irrecoverability if Redwood manages keys; but since we insist on BYOK, we need explicit language that when keys are destroyed by customer, Redwood will follow the documented process and provide logs within 30 days.

Please update the redline to reflect: (i) EU-only residency of primary and backup stores, (ii) BYOK required for EU tenants by default, (iii) deletion request workflow with confirmation within 30 days and backup crypto-erase timeline not to exceed 180 days for archival stores, and (iv) Redwood to provide SOC2 and KMS logs during onboarding and upon reasonable request.

Can you and your team produce the revised clause text today so we can circulate internally?

—Sarah

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-corp.com>, tom.han@acme-corp.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: onshore processing, deletion windows and backups — proposed compromise language

Sarah / Tom — thanks for the quick review. Attached is an updated clause excerpt (embedded in RDW-response-dpa-proposal.docx) with edits that reflect Acme's preferences for BYOK and EU residency. Key points we propose for the DPA: 

1) Residency: "Redwood will ensure that Primary Data and Backups for Customer EU Tenants are stored and processed only within the European Economic Area (EEA) unless Customer provides prior written consent to the contrary."

2) Keys: "Customer will have the option to provide Customer Managed Keys (BYOK) for EU Tenants. Where Customer elects BYOK, Redeeming/Destruction of customer keys by Customer will be treated as a deletion request and Redwood will execute the deletion workflow and provide deletion evidence as set forth below."

3) Deletion workflow & timelines: "Upon Customer's deletion request or expiration of the Service, Redwood shall: (a) logically delete Primary Data within 48 hours, (b) make backups and snapshots inaccessible within 30 days, and (c) render backups cryptographically irrecoverable no later than 180 days (or sooner where Customer destroys BYOK and requests cryptographic erasure). Redwood shall provide a deletion confirmation package (time-stamped logs and signed attestation) within 30 calendar days of the deletion request."

4) Evidence: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II reports and KMS event logs during onboarding and on reasonable request; for specific deletion requests Redwood will furnish key-event log extracts and a signed attestation.

If that language is acceptable, we'll produce a redline-ready DPA (DocuSign package) and propose formal signature routing next week. If you prefer slightly shorter backup irrecoverability windows (e.g., 90 days), we are open to discussing in exchange for additional onboarding escrow controls.

Please review the attached updated draft and let me know if legal needs a tracked-changes DPA or if the excerpt above is sufficient to move forward. I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope once we have alignment.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-response-dpa-proposal.docx (updated clause excerpt, 12KB)
